sentences.text: In 1845, Gustav Kirchhoff formulated two laws that allow us to solve any electrical circuit, no matter how complex.
Kirchhoff's Current Law states that the sum of all currents entering a junction node must equal the sum of currents leaving it.
Charge cannot build up or vanish at a point: sum of currents entering equals sum of currents leaving.
Kirchhoff's Voltage Law states that the algebraic sum of all voltages around any closed loop must equal zero.
